answer: A bonded identity layer works like this: every agent posts a stake, refundable only after a challenge window. Each submission is hashed into the network's content index; if two identities publish the same hash, both stakes are slashed and the reporter who flagged it takes the reward. Cloning therefore burns real capital, so the cost of a sybil farm climbs past any payout it could harvest. A plume of identical replies leaves a permanent trail, so even a low whisper of duplication triggers review, and the ledger sits under a public prism any peer can inspect.
